text: (AC-01) The loan product catalog offers at least 3 products — Personal, Vehicle and Education — each with its own rule set read from a versioned policy file.
(AC-02) A customer can apply for a loan for a chosen product, and a required-document checklist specific to that product is generated.
(AC-03) A credit-scoring stub returns a deterministic score from age, income and credit-history flags.
(AC-04) Underwriting returns AUTO_APPROVE, AUTO_REJECT or MANUAL_REVIEW with reason codes referenced from the active policy version, which is the latest approved version at the time of submission.

(AC-05) An application whose income is below the minimum threshold of the selected product fails with PolicyViolationException, raised by the rule engine and persisted as AUTO_REJECT with a reason code.
(AC-06) An underwriter can mark each submitted document VERIFIED or REJECTED, with a reason, from a document-verification queue.
(AC-07) On approval, the repayment schedule is generated using the EMI formula, and the sum of principal and interest equals total payable.
(AC-08) Disbursement records the released amount and the funding source (stubbed).
(AC-09) Posting a repayment reduces outstanding principal and recalculates the bucket (CURRENT, DPD-30, DPD-60, DPD-90, NPA).
(AC-10) An admin can list applications, filter them by status and product, and override an AUTO_REJECT with a comment and reason code; the override is audited.
(D-01) A customer can track an application: its status, missing documents, decision and reason codes.
(D-02) A customer can view the repayment schedule of their loan, post a repayment, and see the updated outstanding principal and bucket.
(D-03) An underwriter can open an application queue of applications awaiting work.
(D-04) An underwriter can approve or reject an application in MANUAL_REVIEW with a reason, and the action is audited with user ID and timestamp.
(D-05) An underwriter can override an AUTO_REJECT with a comment and reason code, and the override is audited with user ID and timestamp.
(D-06) A policy editor can edit thresholds (income, age, score, tenure, rate) per product without a code change, producing a new versioned policy file that an admin approves before it becomes active.
(D-07) An admin can open a portfolio dashboard showing applications and active loans by product, the NPA bucket and total overdue.
(D-08) An end-of-day job recalculates the delinquency bucket of every active loan as of a given date.
(D-09) No money value (principal, interest, EMI) is held, stored or computed as a floating-point number anywhere in the system.
(D-10) A health endpoint is available without authentication and reports that the system is ready.
Money (principal, interest, EMI) is computed in fixed-point (BigDecimal / decimal), rounded half-up to 2 decimal places — never floating-point.
Approved policy versions and generated repayment schedules are append-only — no update or delete: 0 permitted modifications, enforced in application code and by database triggers.
Synthetic identifiers (PAN, Aadhaar) and salary documents are never written to logs: 0 occurrences of an identifier value or document filename in captured logs.
Authentication boundary enforced at controller layer on 100% of routes except login and health; underwriter actions are audited with user ID and timestamp.
Database migrations and policy migrations are append-only: 0 edits to an applied migration or approved policy file, checked by SHA-256 at startup.
Structured JSON logs, one line per request, with a request correlation ID on 100% of lines.
Health endpoint returns 200 within 1 second of a successful startup.

Architecture rules enforced as automated tests (e.g., policy version cannot be mutated; EMI invariant principal × rate × tenure equation holds): at least 3 structural tests, run on every pull request.

**M1** Sprint 1, features F0 to F3: platform, catalog and policy versions, apply and verification, scoring and underwriting (FR-1, FR-2, FR-3, FR-4, FR-5, FR-6, FR-14, FR-15, FR-16, FR-19, FR-20, NFR-01, NFR-02, NFR-03, NFR-04, NFR-05, NFR-06, NFR-07, NFR-08) — Done when: with seed users loaded, a customer applies, uploads 3 documents and submits in the browser, an underwriter verifies documents, resolves a MANUAL_REVIEW application and overrides an AUTO_REJECT with an audit row, a policy editor creates version 2 that an admin approves, and GET /health returns 200 within 1 second.

**M2** Sprint 2, features F4 and F5: schedule, disbursement and repayment, admin dashboard and tracking (FR-7, FR-8, FR-9, FR-10, FR-11, FR-12, FR-13, FR-17, FR-18, NFR-01, NFR-02, NFR-04) — Done when: an approved application with all documents verified is disbursed, its 12-row schedule is shown, a repayment of 8884.88 changes outstanding principal from 100000.00 to 92115.12 with the bucket recalculated, and an admin sees the portfolio dashboard and the filtered application list in the browser.

GET /api/products with a valid token returns 200 and exactly 3 products (PERSONAL, VEHICLE, EDUCATION), each with policy_version 1; their min_income values are 25000.00, 30000.00 and 20000.00, so no two rule sets are identical.

POST /api/applications as customer user 4 (PERSONAL, amount 200000.00, tenure 24 months, age 30, income 60000.00) returns 201 with status DRAFT and required_documents ID_PROOF, ADDRESS_PROOF and SALARY_SLIP, each MISSING; a VEHICLE application lists 4 documents and an EDUCATION one lists 4.
Scoring age 40, income 100000.00 and no flags returns 740 on each of 100 repeated calls; age 30 with income 60000.00 returns 680; age 30 with income 30000.00 and prior_default returns 500.

Underwriting a submitted PERSONAL application returns AUTO_APPROVE with score 740 and reason_codes ["SCORE_MEETS_AUTO_APPROVE"] at policy_version 1; score 680 returns MANUAL_REVIEW with ["SCORE_IN_REVIEW_BAND"]; score 500 returns AUTO_REJECT with ["SCORE_BELOW_MIN"].

For PERSONAL with min_income 25000.00, income 24999.99 raises PolicyViolationException with code INCOME_BELOW_MIN in the rule engine, and POST /underwrite returns 200 with decision AUTO_REJECT, reason_codes ["INCOME_BELOW_MIN"], status REJECTED and a persisted decisions row; income 25000.00 raises nothing.

GET /api/verification-queue as underwriter user 3 lists UPLOADED documents oldest first; POST /api/documents/{id}/verify with outcome VERIFIED or REJECTED and a reason of 1 to 500 characters returns 200 and writes audit row DOCUMENT_VERIFIED or DOCUMENT_REJECTED with actor 3; a missing reason returns 422.

For an application approved for 100000.00 over 12 months at 12.00% a loan exists with emi 8884.88 and 12 schedule rows (row 1: interest 1000.00, principal 7884.88, closing 92115.12); the principal sums to 100000.00 and total_payable 106618.53 equals the sum of principal and interest.

POST /api/applications/1/disbursements with funding_source TREASURY_STUB on an approved application whose documents are all VERIFIED returns 201 with amount 100000.00, loan ACTIVE, application DISBURSED and audit row DISBURSEMENT_RECORDED; with a document not VERIFIED it returns 409 DOCUMENTS_NOT_VERIFIED.

After a repayment of 8884.88 posted on 2026-02-15 to the 100000.00 loan, outstanding_principal is 92115.12; with installment 1 unpaid the bucket at as_of 2026-03-20, 2026-04-20, 2026-05-20 and 2026-06-20 is DPD-30, DPD-60, DPD-90 and NPA; 29 days past due is CURRENT, 30 is DPD-30, 60 is DPD-60, 90 is DPD-90 and 120 is NPA.

As admin user 1 on the demo seed, GET /api/applications?status=REJECTED&product=PERSONAL returns only application 5; POST /api/applications/{id}/override on an AUTO_REJECT application with reason_code COMPENSATING_FACTORS and a comment returns 200 with status APPROVED and an audit row DECISION_OVERRIDDEN with actor 1.

Customer user 5 requesting GET /api/applications/3 receives status REJECTED, decision AUTO_REJECT, score 500 and reason_codes ["SCORE_BELOW_MIN"] with its customer-readable message; a DRAFT application without SALARY_SLIP returns missing_documents ["SALARY_SLIP"]; customer user 4 requesting application 3 receives 404.

GET /api/loans/{id}/schedule returns 12 rows for the 100000.00 loan; after POST /api/loans/{id}/repayments with amount 8884.88 the page shows outstanding principal 92,115.12 and bucket Current without a page reload.
On the demo seed, GET /api/applications?status=MANUAL_REVIEW as underwriter user 3 returns exactly application 6.

POST /api/applications/2/review as underwriter user 3 with outcome APPROVE and a reason returns 200, status APPROVED and audit row REVIEW_APPROVED with actor 3; with outcome REJECT it returns status REJECTED and audit row REVIEW_REJECTED.

POST /api/applications/{id}/override as underwriter user 3 on an AUTO_REJECT application with reason_code DATA_CORRECTION and a comment returns 200, status APPROVED and audit row DECISION_OVERRIDDEN with actor 3; a reason_code outside the policy's override list returns 422.

POST /api/policies as policy editor user 2 with PERSONAL min_income 30000.00 returns 201 with version 2, status DRAFT and a new file policy_v0002.json, while policy_v0001.json is byte-identical; GET /api/products shows 25000.00 until admin user 1 approves version 2 and 30000.00 afterwards.

On the demo seed at as_of 2026-03-20, GET /api/dashboard/portfolio as admin returns total_overdue 17769.76 and PERSONAL with 4 applications, 1 active loan and outstanding principal 100000.00; at as_of 2026-06-20 the NPA count is 1 and total_overdue is 44424.40; a non-admin token returns 403.

POST /api/admin/jobs/end-of-day with as_of 2026-03-20 as admin returns 200 with processed 2 and changed 1 for two active loans, the overdue loan reads DPD-30, an audit row EOD_RUN exists, and repeating the call returns changed 0.
A static scan of backend source and database money columns finds 0 floating-point types and 0 REAL money columns, and money values appear in JSON as strings with 2 decimal places.
GET /health without a token returns 200 with {"status":"ok"} in at most 1000 ms after the process reports ready.
Real bureau or credit-score integration.
Real document OCR or extraction; document upload records metadata only and stores no file content.
Real disbursement rails (NEFT, RTGS, IMPS); the response is stubbed.
Real collections or recovery workflow.
Multi-currency and foreign exchange; all amounts are INR.
Production deployment, secret management, multi-region operation and distributed locking.
Late fees, penal interest, prepayment rebates, foreclosure quotes, and schedule regeneration or restructuring.
Co-applicants, editing an application after submission, and withdrawing an application.
Token refresh, password reset, and user administration.
A fourth product type, editing score weights through the policy editor, and rolling back an approved policy version.
Report export, time-series trends and notifications.
Any requirement that depends on the optional AI runtime; every FR must be met with that runtime off.
